[{"id":"f-indemn-93657a14","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a","rationale":"The Agreement contains no indemnification, defence or hold-harmless provision anywhere: Section 9 (Warranties) ends with the Globix acknowledgement and is followed immediately by Section 10 (General Provisions), and there is no limitation-of-liability article either. Searches for indemnify/indemnification, hold harmless and IP-infringement language return nothing; the only third-party IP reference (Section 7.2) is a mutual advertising covenant, not an indemnity. HDI designs, develops, hosts and operates the Site and holds a licence to our Marks, so the total absence of an HDI IP-infringement indemnity is walk-away territory under this rule. We have therefore inserted a preferred-level HDI indemnity (IP infringement, breach of law, HDI-caused data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with the standard notice, control and cooperation procedure, plus a narrow Company indemnity confined to Company-provided Content and our own breach of law. We did not add the fallback three-times-annual-fees super-cap, which would only serve to cap HDI's exposure in an agreement that currently has no liability cap.","proposal":"Insert HDI indemnity (IP, breach of law, data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with claim procedure and a narrow Company indemnity.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-02ea966e","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a","rationale":"Section 10.3 is captioned \"Assignment\" but is only a binding-effect/successors-and-assigns clause: it neither confirms our right to assign to an affiliate or successor nor restricts HDI, so HDI is free to transfer this Agreement (potentially to a leather-goods competitor) without our consent. No change-of-control termination or re-pricing right exists anywhere (the only termination triggers are Section 2 non-renewal/notice and the Section 1 delivery-failure right), so we are not in walk-away territory, but the clause fails every fallback element (successor assignment, notice, consent for other assignments, reasonableness standard). We have therefore taken the fallback rather than the asymmetric preferred position: one short mutual provision permitting successor assignment on written notice and requiring not-unreasonably-withheld consent for any other assignment, leaving Section 10.3 otherwise untouched.","proposal":"Add mutual successor-assignment right with notice and a not-unreasonably-withheld consent standard for other assignments","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-2dd2a8a6","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a","rationale":"Section 6.1 imposes exclusive dealing on the Company: for the entire term it may not participate in any similar Internet project for Deerskin Products or substantially similar products, and HDI additionally takes the exclusive right to use the Company's own \"Deerskin\" brand for a direct-to-consumer web site. The term runs one year and renews automatically on each anniversary (Section 4.1), so the restriction is open-ended, and there is no automatic performance-based exit — Section 1.6 gives only a discretionary termination right if the Site is not live in 70 days, which does not end exclusivity automatically on service-level or delivery-date failure. The only carve-out (Section 6.2, closeout merchandise) does not narrow the covenant to a 12-month, exit-linked exclusivity. That is walk-away territory (exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance-based exit), so it fails the fallback. We therefore take the preferred position and replace the covenant with a no-exclusivity statement, which also removes HDI's exclusive hold on our own brand; HDI's reciprocal restriction in Section 6.3 benefits us and is left in place.","proposal":"Replace the Company-side exclusivity covenant and HDI's exclusive Deerskin brand right in Section 6.1 with a no-exclusivity statement.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-61adaf34","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a","rationale":"Section 6.1 imposes a non-compete and field-of-use restriction on us: we may not participate in any project similar to the Site with respect to Deerskin Products or any \"products substantially similar\" (an open-ended category expressly extending to \"companies similar to\" named competitors), and HDI additionally takes an exclusive right over our own \"Deerskin\" brand for direct-to-consumer Internet sales. This fails the fallback on several material terms: the scope is not a single named competing product; the only carve-out (Section 6.2) is limited to closeout \"Deerskin\" merchandise, with no carve-out for our internal development or for acquisitions; and although the covenant runs \"during the term of this Agreement\", the term auto-renews annually under Section 4.1, so the restriction is not capped at 12 months. Because HDI's retained exclusive right would still prevent us from using or licensing our own brand, we have taken the preferred position and removed both the Company covenant and the exclusivity in Section 6.1, leaving Section 6.2 and HDI's own restriction in Section 6.3 untouched.","proposal":"Remove the Company non-compete and HDI's exclusive \"Deerskin\" brand right in Section 6.1","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-t4c-2a593435","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and","rationale":"Section 4.1's 90-day termination right sits grammatically inside the auto-renewal sentence, so the Company's convenience exit is open to being read as a non-renewal mechanic only; we therefore state the Company's convenience right in a standalone operative sentence at the fallback notice period (90 days). Two further fallback elements fail: (i) HDI's right is not tied to the end of the then-current term (its notice may fix any Termination Date), so HDI could walk away mid-term; and (ii) the Termination Payment triggered by the Company's termination is uncapped (aggregate Net Sales for the preceding twelve months less $800,000, divided by two, payable in eight quarterly instalments) and can far exceed three months of fees. Section 3 (\"Fees; Payment\", § 3.1) confirms the consideration runs from the Company to HDI as 30% of Net Sales, so the cap on \"amounts payable by the Company to HDI under Section 3\" is neither nil nor undefined. HDI's 90-day notice period is already met. The preferred 30-day notice and pro-rata refund of prepaid fees are accepted shortfalls given the fallback is reached, and are not redlined.","proposal":"Add a standalone Company right to terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice, limit HDI's termination to the end of the then-current term, and cap the Termination Payment at three months' Section 3 amounts.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-audit-8c7da5d6","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and","rationale":"Section 3.4 is the only provision binding the Company to an audit/inspection right (no other audit, records or verification clause exists in the Agreement). It already meets two fallback elements on their material terms: inspections require no less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice (exceeding the 15-day floor) and HDI bears the inspection cost unconditionally (better than \"unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent\"); it is also limited to payment-calculation records during normal business hours. But it imposes no frequency limit, so HDI could inspect repeatedly, failing the fallback once-per-year element and edging toward walk-away territory. We propose the single minimal edit adding a once-per-year cap. We have not pursued the preferred independent-auditor, confidentiality, off-site or no-systems-access elements, as fallback is the selected target and the notice and cost terms already sit at or above it.","proposal":"Cap HDI's records inspection right at once per year in §3.4.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-f066f147","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a","rationale":"Section 10.5 selects New York law, which matches our preferred governing law. However, the Agreement contains no dispute forum provision anywhere: searches for arbitration, jurisdiction, venue and courts return nothing, and the General Provisions article ends at Section 10.8 immediately before the signature block. The forum half of the rule therefore fails at both preferred and fallback level (no corresponding court designation at all), leaving venue open to any forum a party chooses. This is not walk-away territory (no foreign law or offshore arbitration), so we add only the shortest exclusive-forum sentence at the preferred level, with the customary temporary injunctive relief carve-out, and leave the existing New York choice-of-law wording untouched.","proposal":"Add exclusive New York County forum to the existing New York governing law clause.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-e652efed","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and","rationale":"Section 4.2 imposes a stipulated Customer-payable termination amount: on any termination by the Company (including non-renewal under Section 4.1), the Company owes half of trailing twelve-month Net Sales in excess of $800,000, payable in eight quarterly instalments. That is a liquidated amount payable by us with no cap, and because our fees to HDI are only 30% of Net Sales above $11,000 per month, the formula can greatly exceed three months' fees. It therefore fails the fallback (early-termination fee capped at three months' fees as the sole liquidated amount). Deleting Section 4.2 outright to reach the preferred position would require collateral rewrites of the Section 4 heading and the zero-floor and instalment mechanics, so we take the fallback: a single added proviso caps the Termination Payment at the fees payable for the three months preceding the Termination Date and confirms it is the only liquidated amount or penalty we owe. The existing zero-floor in Section 4.2(b), which benefits us, is preserved.","proposal":"Cap the Termination Payment at three months' fees and make it the sole liquidated amount payable by the Company","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-7c1ccaa1","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and","rationale":"The only grant of rights to us is Section 1.4 (access to, and the right to use, HDI's hosting system and HDI's software and Content administration tools). It runs to \"the Company\" alone — \"Company\" is defined in the preamble as The Deerskin Companies, Inc. only, so affiliates are not included and there is no path to add them, which fails the fallback element on affiliate coverage. Successor transfer is satisfied on its material terms by Section 10.3, under which the Agreement inures to the benefit of and is enforceable by the parties' successors and assigns without HDI consent, so no change is needed there. The grant is not revocable at HDI's discretion, so this is not walk-away territory; we therefore make the single shortest fallback-level change (affiliates on written notice) and do not press the preferred perpetual/irrevocable and contractor language.","proposal":"Extend the Section 1.4 access/use rights to Company affiliates on written notice","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mfn-b29b297f","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no most-favoured-nation obligation on the Company. The only \"no less favorably\" covenant (Section 1.8, p0013–p0014) runs in our favour: HDI must promote the Site and Deerskin Products no less favorably than its own catalog titles, at HDI's cost. The fee mechanic (Section 3.1, p0019) is a fixed 30% of Net Sales above a monthly threshold with no obligation to match or extend to HDI any better terms given to third parties, and there is no right-to-match, best-price disclosure, or benchmarking mechanic anywhere in the document. Section 6 (p0037) is an exclusivity/brand restriction, not an MFN, and is assessed under the exclusivity rule rather than flagged twice here. This sits at the preferred position (no Customer MFN), so no redline is proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-9158be5e","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and","rationale":"This sits at the preferred position. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.2 (Deerskin / HDI Agreement)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.2 — verified findings and recommended positions

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Agreement on behalf of the Company (Customer). The document is unusually thin on ri[REDACTED] architecture: it contains **no indemnification provision, no limitation of liability, no performance warranty, no IP/ownership allocation, no insurance covenant and no post-termination transition or data-return mechanic**. HDI designs, develops, hosts and operates the Site, holds a licence to our Marks, and holds our Content and customer/user data on its own server, so these gaps sit squarely against us.

Three issues are the commercial priorities:

1. **No HDI IP-infringement indemnity (critical, missing).** Section 9 (Warranties) runs straight into Section 10 (General Provisions); the only third-party IP reference (Section 7.2) is a mutual advertising covenant. We have inserted a preferred-level HDI indemnity with claim procedure, plus a narrow Company indemnity limited to Company-provided Content and our own breach of law. We deliberately did **not** add a super-cap, which would only benefit HDI in an agreement with no liability cap.
2. **Exclusivity and non-compete on the Company (high).** Section 6.1 bars us from any similar Internet project for Deerskin Products or "substantially similar" products for the full auto-renewing term, and hands HDI the exclusive right to use our own "Deerskin" brand for direct-to-consumer web sales. There is no automatic performance-based exit (Section 1.6 is a discretionary 70-day right only) and the sole carve-out (Section 6.2, closeout merchandise) is too narrow. We take the preferred position and replace the covenant with a no-exclusivity statement; HDI's reciprocal restriction in Section 6.3 benefits us and stays.
3. **Exit economics (high).** The Section 4.2 Termination Payment — half of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000, in eight quarterly instalments — is uncapped and can far exceed three months' fees (fees are 30% of Net Sales under Section 3.1). We cap it at three months' Section 3 amounts and confirm it is the sole liquidated amount we owe, and we restate the Company's convenience right as a standalone sentence (it currently sits inside the auto-renewal sentence in Section 4.1) while limiting HDI's termination to the end of the then-current term.

Three rules are **compliant at the preferred position** and require no redline: no Customer MFN (Section 1.8's "no less favorably" covenant runs in our favour), no minimum purchase or volume commitment (pure revenue share above an $11,000 monthly floor), and no non-solicitation binding the Company.

Remaining medium and low items — audit frequency, dispute forum, licence scope for affiliates, renewal notice window, warranty, transition/data return, insurance, IP and liability cap — are addressed at the fallback level with the shortest workable edits, as noted in the table below.

---

## 2. Findings

| Sev. | Rule | Status | Section | Position / proposal |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 5.4 (as marked) | Insert HDI indemnity (IP, breach of law, HDI-caused data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with notice, control and cooperation procedure; narrow Company indemnity for Company-provided Content and our breach of law. No super-cap volunteered. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 5.4 (as marked); Section 10.3 | Section 10.3 is successors-and-assigns only and does not restrict HDI. Add one mutual provision: successor assignment on written notice; consent not unreasonably withheld for other assignments (fallback). |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 5.4 (as marked); Sections 6.1–6.3, 4.1, 1.6 | Full-term exclusive dealing with no automatic performance-based exit — walk-away territory. Replace the Company covenant and HDI's exclusive "Deerskin" brand right with a no-exclusivity statement (preferred); Section 6.3 retained. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 5.4 (as marked); Sections 6.1, 6.2, 4.1 | Open-ended "substantially similar products" scope, no internal-development or acquisition carve-out, not capped at 12 months due to annual auto-renewal. Remove the Company covenant and HDI's exclusive brand right (preferred); Sections 6.2 and 6.3 untouched. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation *(verification: repaired)* | § 1.4 (as marked); Sections 4.1, 4.2, 3.1 | Standalone Company convenience right on 90 days' notice (fallback); limit HDI's termination to the end of the then-current term; cap the Termination Payment at three months' Section 3 amounts. Preferred 30-day notice and pro-rata refund not pressed. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 (as marked); Section 3.4 | Notice (30 days) and cost allocation already at or above fallback; no frequency limit. Single edit: cap inspections at once per year. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 5.4 (as marked); Section 10.5 | New York law matches preferred; no forum provision anywhere. Add one exclusive New York County forum sentence with temporary injunctive relief carve-out; choice-of-law wording untouched. |
| Medium | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 (as marked); Sections 4.1, 4.2 | Uncapped stipulated exit amount. Add a proviso capping the Termination Payment at fees payable for the three months preceding the Termination Date and confirming it is the sole liquidated amount or penalty. Section 4.2(b) zero-floor preserved (favourable). |
| Medium | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 1.4 (as marked); Sections 1.4, 10.3 | Grant runs to "the Company" only (preamble definition excludes affiliates). Successor transfer already satisfied by Section 10.3. Single fallback edit: extend access/use rights to Company affiliates on written notice. |
| Medium | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | **Compliant (preferred)** | § 1.4 (as marked); Sections 1.8, 3.1 | No Customer MFN; the "no less favorably" covenant in Section 1.8 runs in our favour. No redline. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | **Compliant (preferred)** | § 1.4 (as marked); Sections 3.1, 1.2, 1.6, 1.8, 2.2 | Pure revenue share above an $11,000 monthly floor; no minimum spend, take-or-pay or volume cap. | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Compliant (preferred)** | § 5.4 (as marked) | No solicitation, hiring or no-hire restriction on the Company anywhere. Noted for the file: we likewise have no non-solicit protection against HDI, and the playbook does not require us to introduce one. No redline. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal / non-renewal notice | Deviation | § 1.4 (as marked); Section 4.1 | 90-day non-renewal window exceeds the 60-day fallback maximum. | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 1.4 (as marked); Sections 4, 1.4/1.5, 8 | No effects-of-termination, transition, export or deletion mechanic; access and export files exist only during the term. Insert fallback clause: at least 90 days' transition assistance and data export within 30 days of expiry or termination. Preferred six-month/certified-deletion package not pressed. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 5.4 (as marked); Section 9 | Section 9 is corporate authority plus the Globix acknowledgement only; no performance warranty or remedy. Insert fallback warranty: 90-day documentation conformance for the Site and HDI software, 30-day services conformance, repair/replacement or refund at the Company's election. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 5.4 (as marked); Sections 10.1–10.8 | No insurance covenant despite HDI hosting the Site and processing our user and order data. Insert fallback clause: E&O USD 1,000,000; cyber and privacy USD 2,000,000. CGL, workers' compensation and certificate mechanics not pursued. |
| Low | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Missing | § 5.4 (as marked); Section 6.1 | No IP allocation; only a narrow Marks licence. Insert Section 5.5 at fallback: HDI retains generic tools and know-how; Company receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Site and deliverables; HDI's licence in Company data limited to providing the Services. Preferred assignment of the Site not pushed given HDI bears development costs under Section 1.2. |
| Low | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Missing | § 5.4 (as marked); Sections 1–10, 10.2 | No cap, exclusive remedy or consequential-damages exclusion; both parties uncapped. Insert new Section 10.9 at fallback: mutual cap at fees paid or payable by the Company in the preceding 12 months, with confidentiality, indemnification, gross negligence and wilful misconduct uncapped. Preferred floor and additional carve-outs held in reserve. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These are the points our findings place in walk-away territory. We should not sign without movement on them.

1. **Absence of an HDI IP-infringement indemnity (INDEMN, critical).** HDI designs, develops, hosts and operates the Site and licenses our Marks; the total absence of an IP indemnity is walk-away territory under the rule. There is also no limitation of liability to soften it.
2. **Section 6.1 exclusivity (EXCLUSIVITY, high).** Exclusive dealing for the full auto-renewing term with no automatic performance-based exit is walk-away territory. HDI's exclusive hold on our own "Deerskin" brand for direct-to-consumer web sales compounds this.
3. **Absence of any insurance covenant (INSURANCE, low severity but flagged).** For a vendor that processes our Content, user information and customer order data, the absence of coverage sits in walk-away territory under the rule.

Near the line, and worth watching in negotiation:

- **Section 3.4 audit with no frequency limit** — edges toward walk-away territory; the once-per-year cap is a minimal ask.
- **90-day non-renewal notice window** — at the edge of walk-away territory under the renewal rule.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** reflecting the proposals above: the HDI indemnity, the no-exclusivity replacement for Section 6.1, the Termination Payment cap and standalone convenience right, the IP section, the mutual liability cap, the warranty, the transition/data-export clause, the insurance covenant and the exclusive New York forum sentence, plus the short edits to Sections 1.4 (affiliates), 3.4 (once per year), 4.1 (60-day Company notice) and 10.3 (mutual assignment).
2. **Lead with the three walk-away items** in the first negotiation session — indemnity, Section 6.1 exclusivity, and insurance — and treat the remaining fallback-level edits as a package to be closed together.
3. **Confirm the exit maths with the business team**: quantify the Section 4.2 formula (half of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000) against expected Net Sales so we can show HDI the exposure the three-month cap is addressing.
4. **Hold in reserve** the preferred positions we have not pressed (30-day convenience notice and pro-rata refund; 12-month software warranty and no-malicious-code; six-month transition with certified deletion; USD 1,000,000 liability floor and the wider carve-out set; assignment of the Site) for use if HDI resists the fallback package.
5. **Note for the file**: the T4C finding is marked as verification "repaired"; we will re-check that clause's final wording against Sections 4.1, 4.2 and 3.1 before the redline goes out.
6. **Flag internally** that the Agreement contains no non-solicit protection running against HDI. This is compliant under our playbook and we are not proposing to introduce one, but the business should be aware.
"}

2. **Section 6.1 exclusivity (EXCLUSIVITY, high).** Exclusive dealing for the full auto-renewing term with no automatic performance-based exit is walk-away territory. HDI's exclusive hold on our own "Deerskin" brand for direct-to-consumer web sales compounds this.
3. **Absence of any insurance covenant (INSURANCE, low severity but flagged).** For a vendor that processes our Content, user information and customer order data, the absence of coverage sits in walk-away territory under the rule.

Near the line, and worth watching in negotiation:

- **Section 3.4 audit with no frequency limit** — edges toward walk-away territory; the once-per-year cap is a minimal ask.
- **90-day non-renewal notice window** — at the edge of walk-away territory under the renewal rule.
